chunks: ʿAlī narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a man whom two men brought and said, “This man stole a coat of mail.” As the evidence was being examined, the man kept imploring him and saying, “By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had been here, he would never have cut off my hand.”

He said, “Why?” The man said, “His Lord would inform him that I am innocent, and he would declare me innocent because of my innocence.” He said: when he saw the man’s earnest imploring of him, he called the two witnesses and said, “Fear Allah, and do not cut off the man’s hand unjustly,” and he adjured them. Then he said, “Let one of you cut off his hand, and let the other hold his hand.”

So when they came forward to the platform to cut off his hand, he caused the people to be struck so that they became mixed together. Then, when they had mixed together, the two men let the accused man go into the midst of the crowd when the people had become intermingled.

Then the man against whom they had testified came and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the two men testified against me unjustly. When the people were struck and became mixed together, they let me go and fled. Had they been truthful, they would not have let me go.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said, “Who will show me where these two are, so that I may punish them as a deterrent?”

key_terms.أُنَكِّلْهُمَا: I will punish them in a way that serves as a deterrent
key_terms.بَرِيءٌ: innocent and free of the accusation
key_terms.دِرْعًا: a coat of mail alleged to have been stolen
key_terms.ٱتَّقِيَا ٱللَّهَ: an admonition to fear Allah before testifying or acting
key_terms.ٱلْبَيِّنَةِ: the evidentiary proof examined in a legal case

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام deal with false witnesses in a theft case?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a judicial case in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام handled an accusation of theft with caution and scrutiny. It highlights the gravity of witness testimony in hadd cases and shows his concern to prevent ظلم before an irreversible punishment was carried out.
